info.name: Health Center API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Health Center server application.

This collection covers all available REST API endpoints organized by feature module:
- **Auth** – Patient and Admin authentication
- **Centers** – Health center management
- **Doctors** – Doctor profiles and availability
- **Slots** – Doctor appointment slot browsing
- **Doctor Appointments** – Channeling appointment booking and management
- **Prescriptions** – Doctor-issued prescriptions and pharmacy dispensing
- **Admin – Doctor Management** – Admin CRUD and slot control for doctors
- **Lab – Diagnostic Tests** – Catalogue of lab/diagnostic tests
- **Lab – Appointment Slots** – Lab slot generation and retrieval
- **Lab – Bookings** – Lab appointment booking management
- **Test Types** – Test type definitions (alias of Diagnostic Tests)
- **Test Results** – Patient lab result entry and retrieval
- **Pharmacy – Medication Inventory** – Medicine stock and batch management
- **Pharmacy – Orders** – Pharmacy order processing

**Base URL:** `{{base_url}}` (default: http://localhost:8081)

**Authentication:** Most protected routes expect a JWT Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Admin routes additionally require the `admin` or `superadmin` role.

**Session-based routes** (Doctor routes `/api/doctors/me`, `/api/appointments/doctor/me`) use a session cookie set after the doctor logs in via `/api/auth/login`.

variable.description: Base URL of the Health Center API server
JWT Bearer token obtained from login endpoints. Set this after logging in.
JWT Bearer token for admin/superadmin. Set this after admin login.

item.name: Auth – User / Patient
item.description:
Handles patient registration, login, profile retrieval, profile updates, password change, and logout.

All protected routes require a `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` header with a valid JWT token obtained from the login endpoint.

request.description:
Creates a new patient account.

All four fields are required. Returns a JWT token and the created user object on success. Returns 400 if the email is already registered.

Authenticates a user (patient, doctor, receptionist, or pharmacy staff) and returns a JWT token.

Store the returned `token` in the `{{token}}` collection variable for use in protected requests. For doctor logins the server also sets a session cookie.
Invalidates the current user session and/or JWT. Call this to log out a user. No request body is required.

Returns the authenticated patient's profile information. Requires a valid JWT Bearer token.

Returns the user object including fullName, phone, email, and role.
Updates the authenticated patient's profile fields. Only include fields you want to change. Requires a valid JWT Bearer token.
Changes the authenticated user's password. Both `currentPassword` and `newPassword` are required. Returns 400 if the current password is incorrect.

item.name: Auth – Admin
item.description:
Handles admin account registration, login, and profile retrieval.

Admin accounts support multiple roles: `admin`, `superadmin`, `lab-tech`, and `center-admin`. Protected routes require `Authorization: Bearer {{admin_token}}`. Only `admin` or `superadmin` can register new admins.

request.description:
Creates a new admin account. The `role` field is optional and defaults to `superadmin`. Valid roles: `admin`, `superadmin`, `lab-tech`, `center-admin`.

This is typically used to bootstrap the first admin account manually.

Authenticates an admin by email and password. Returns a JWT token and admin profile.

Store the `token` value in `{{admin_token}}` for use in admin-protected routes.
Returns the authenticated admin's profile. Accessible by roles: `admin`, `superadmin`, `lab-tech`, `center-admin`.
Simple health-check endpoint for the admin auth route. Returns `{ ok: true }` if the server is running and routes are mounted correctly. No authentication required.

item.name: Centers
item.description:
Manages health center records. Public endpoints allow visiting users to browse active centers and featured centers. Admin endpoints (requiring `admin` or `superadmin` role) support full CRUD and toggling visibility.

All admin routes require `Authorization: Bearer {{admin_token}}`.

request.description:
Returns all active health centers visible to the public. No authentication required.

Each center includes name, address, district, opening/closing times, and active status.
Returns health centers marked as featured. Used on the homepage / landing page to highlight key centers. No authentication required.
Returns all health centers regardless of active or featured status. Intended for admin management views. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.
Creates a new health center. `name`, `openingTime`, and `closingTime` are required. Times must be in `HH:mm` format. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.
Partially updates fields on a health center. Include only the fields you want to change. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.
Toggles the `isActive` flag of a health center. Deactivating a center hides it from public listing. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.
Toggles the `isFeatured` flag of a health center. Featured centers appear in the `/api/centers/featured` public listing. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.

item.name: Doctors
item.description:
Provides public access to doctor listings and detail pages, and allows logged-in doctors to view and update their own profiles.

Public routes require no authentication. Doctor-specific routes (`/me`) are protected by session middleware and require the `doctor` role. Session is established after login via `/api/auth/login`.

request.description: Returns a list of all active doctors. Can be filtered by specialization, center, or name depending on server implementation. No authentication required.
Returns the full profile of a specific doctor by their MongoDB ObjectId. Includes specialization, clinic, fee, schedule, and center assignment. No authentication required.

Returns the authenticated doctor's own profile. Protected by session middleware; the requesting user must have the `doctor` role.

The session/token is established after the doctor logs in via `/api/auth/login`.
Allows a logged-in doctor to update their own profile fields such as phone or clinic name. Requires `doctor` role via session middleware. Only provided fields are updated.

item.name: Slots – Doctor Availability
item.description:
Provides access to available appointment slots for a specific doctor on a given date.

Slots are auto-generated by the server's rolling slot scheduler based on the doctor's working schedule. This endpoint is public and is used by patients before booking an appointment.

item.name: Get Available Slots for a Doctor

request.description:
Returns all unbooked slots for a specific doctor on the given date. Both `doctorId` and `date` query parameters are required.

Returns 400 if either parameter is missing. Results are sorted by `startTime` ascending.

item.name: Doctor Appointments (Channeling)
item.description:
Manages the full lifecycle of doctor-channeling appointments: booking, viewing, status updates, and cancellation.

Patients can book and cancel appointments. Doctors (protected by session) can view their appointment list and update appointment statuses. Appointments reference a doctor, patient, slot, and center.

request.description:
Books a doctor appointment for a patient. The slot is immediately marked as booked to prevent double-booking. `centerId`, `doctorId`, `userId`, `slotId`, and `payment.amount` are required.

Returns 400 if the slot is already booked.
Returns all appointments for a specific patient, sorted by most recent first. Pass the patient's MongoDB ObjectId as a path parameter.
Returns all appointments assigned to the currently authenticated doctor. Protected by the doctor session middleware. Useful for the doctor's dashboard to see their upcoming and past appointments.

Allows a doctor to update the status of an appointment. Valid statuses: `pending`, `confirmed`, `completed`, `no_show`, `cancelled`. Protected by doctor session middleware.

Only the doctor assigned to the appointment can update its status.
Cancels a doctor appointment and releases the associated slot back to available. Can be called by the patient or admin. Returns 404 if the appointment does not exist.

item.name: Prescriptions
item.description:
Manages doctor-issued prescriptions and pharmacy dispensing. Doctors create prescriptions linked to appointments; patients and pharmacy staff can view and act on them.

All prescription routes require authentication. Each prescription is linked to a doctor, patient, center, and appointment. A PDF download is available for each prescription.

request.description:
Returns prescriptions for the authenticated user. Patients only see their own prescriptions. Doctors see prescriptions they issued. Admins and pharmacy staff see all.

Query parameters such as `userId`, `doctorId`, or `status` may be supported by the controller.
Returns prescriptions created by the currently authenticated doctor. Protected by the doctor session middleware (separate from JWT). Useful for the doctor's prescription history view.
Creates a new prescription for a patient linked to a completed appointment. Only users with the `doctor` role may create prescriptions. A sequential `prescriptionNo` (e.g. P0001) is auto-generated.
Returns the full details of a single prescription including doctor info, patient info, diagnosis, notes, and medication items. Accessible by doctor, patient, pharmacy, admin, and superadmin.
Streams or downloads a PDF version of the prescription. The response Content-Type is `application/pdf`. Accessible by doctor, patient, pharmacy, admin, and superadmin.
Updates the prescription status to `dispensed` and records dispensing details including who dispensed it and any remarks. Only `pharmacy`, `admin`, and `superadmin` roles are authorized.

item.name: Admin – Doctor Management
item.description:
Admin-only endpoints for managing doctor profiles, activating/deactivating doctors, and manually triggering slot generation or cleanup.

All routes in this folder require `Authorization: Bearer {{admin_token}}` with `admin` or `superadmin` role. These endpoints control the doctor roster and the rolling slot scheduler.

request.description: Returns all doctor records including inactive ones. Intended for the admin management panel. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.
Returns the full admin-level view of a doctor including all schedule fields, working days, holiday dates, and slot configuration. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.

Creates a new doctor profile and immediately generates rolling appointment slots based on the provided schedule. `name`, `specialization`, `clinic`, `fee`, `phone`, and `centerId` are required.

`startTime` and `endTime` must be in `HH:mm` format. `sessionTime` is the consultation duration in minutes. `workingDays` accepts mon/tue/wed/thu/fri/sat/sun. After creation, slots are auto-generated for the next 14 days (configurable).
Partially updates a doctor's profile fields. Include only the fields to change. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role. Note: changing schedule fields does not automatically regenerate existing slots.
Enables or disables a doctor's account. Inactive doctors are hidden from the public listing and their unbooked future slots may be deactivated. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.

Manually triggers the rolling slot generation for all active doctors. Generates slots for the next `days` days (default: 14, configured via `DEFAULT_SLOT_WINDOW_DAYS` env var). Useful after setting up new doctors or after a server restart. Requires `admin` or `superadmin` role.
Deactivates all past unbooked slots to keep the database clean. This is normally run automatically by the server's scheduled slot maintenance, but can be triggered manually by an admin.

item.name: Lab – Diagnostic Tests
item.description:
Manages the catalogue of diagnostic/lab tests available at health centers. Each test has a name, description, category, price, sample type, instructions, and optional measurable parameters.

Public routes allow patients to browse available tests. Admin CRUD routes allow creation, updates, and deletion. Currently no authentication middleware is enforced on write routes (open to any caller).

request.description: Returns all diagnostic tests in the catalogue. No authentication required. Used by patients to browse available lab tests and by booking flows to select a test.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the diagnostic test

request.description: Returns the full details of a single diagnostic test by its MongoDB ObjectId, including parameters, sample type, price, and instructions.

Creates a new diagnostic test in the catalogue. `name` is required. `parameters` is an array of measurable result fields (name, unit, normalMinValue, normalMaxValue). A unique `testCode` is auto-generated.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the diagnostic test

request.description: Fully updates a diagnostic test record. Include all required fields alongside any changes. Requires the test's MongoDB ObjectId as a path parameter.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the diagnostic test

request.description: Permanently deletes a diagnostic test from the catalogue. This operation is irreversible. Returns 404 if the test is not found.

item.name: Lab – Appointment Slots
item.description:
Manages lab appointment slots at health centers. Slots define available time windows for patients to book laboratory tests.

Admins can generate, update, and delete slots. Patients can retrieve available slots by center. Note: these routes are mounted directly at the root (no `/api/lab/` prefix) – the full paths are `/api/generateSlots`, `/api/getSlots`, etc. as defined in the route file.

request.description: Generates a batch of appointment slots for a lab center on a specified date. `center` (ObjectId), `slotDate`, `startTime`, and `endTime` are required. Duplicate slots (same center + date + startTime) are prevented by a unique index.
Updates an existing lab appointment slot. Can be used to change the slot's time, status (`AVAILABLE`, `BOOKED`, `CANCELLED`), or linked booking.
Returns all lab appointment slots across all centers. Intended for admin overviews. For a center-specific or availability query use the other get-slots endpoints.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the health center

request.description: Returns all lab appointment slots belonging to a specific health center, regardless of their status. Useful for center-level admin management.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the health center

request.description: Returns only slots with `status: AVAILABLE` for a specific center. Used in the patient booking flow to populate the time-picker with open slots.
Permanently deletes a specific lab appointment slot. Only unbooked slots should be deleted to avoid orphaned bookings. Returns 404 if not found.
Bulk-deletes all past (expired) lab slots that were never booked. Useful for periodic database cleanup. Does not affect booked or cancelled slots.
Bulk-deletes all future lab slots that have not yet been booked. Use with caution – this removes all open capacity for upcoming dates. Typically used when regenerating a fresh slot schedule.

item.name: Lab – Bookings
item.description:
Handles lab appointment bookings for patients at health centers. Each booking links a patient (`user`), a slot, a diagnostic test, and a health center.

These routes are mounted at the root level (no prefix path). Full paths include `/api/bookappointment`, `/api/appointment/:id`, etc. as defined in the router file.

request.description:
Books a lab appointment for a patient. All five fields are required: `user` (patient ObjectId), `slot` (slot ObjectId), `diagnosticTest` (test ObjectId), `healthCenter` (center ObjectId), and `appointmentDate`.

Initial status is `CONFIRMED`. Returns the created booking object.
Returns the full details of a single lab appointment booking including linked user, slot, test, and center information.
Returns all lab bookings made by a specific patient. Used to display a patient's booking history in their dashboard.
Updates an existing lab appointment booking. Can be used to change the status (`CONFIRMED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED`) or reschedule the appointment date.
Permanently deletes a lab appointment booking. Returns 404 if the booking does not exist. Use with caution as this is non-reversible.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the health center

request.description: Returns all lab appointment bookings for a specific health center. Used by center administrators to manage their incoming appointments.
Returns all lab appointment bookings across all health centers. Intended for system-wide admin views and reporting.

item.name: Test Types
item.description:
Manages test type definitions (aliases for `DiagnosticTest`). Both `/api/test-types` and `/api/lab/diagnostic-tests` share the same underlying data collection (`testtypes`). This folder documents the `/api/test-types` route group.

Full CRUD is supported. No authentication middleware is currently enforced on these routes.

request.description: Returns all test type records from the shared diagnostic test collection. Equivalent to `/api/lab/diagnostic-tests`.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the test type

request.description: Returns the full details of a specific test type by MongoDB ObjectId.
Creates a new test type / diagnostic test entry. Writes to the same collection as `/api/lab/diagnostic-tests`. A unique auto-generated `testCode` is assigned.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the test type

request.description: Updates a test type record. Provide the full or partial document to update. Returns the updated document.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the test type

request.description: Permanently deletes a test type by MongoDB ObjectId. Returns 404 if not found.

item.name: Test Results
item.description:
Manages patient lab test results entered by lab technicians. Each result is linked to a lab appointment, test type, patient, and optionally a doctor.

Results include measurable parameter values (name, value, unit, normal range). The overall `condition` can be `normal`, `severe`, or `unknown`. A `recommendConsultation` flag can be set for worrying results.

body.raw:
{
  "appointmentId": "booking001",
  "testTypeId": "664testtype001",
  "patientId": "664patient001",
  "doctorId": "664abc123def456",
  "status": "completed",
  "condition": "normal",
  "results": [
    {
      "name": "Haemoglobin",
      "value": 14.5,
      "unit": "g/dL",
      "normalMinValue": 12,
      "normalMaxValue": 17
    },
    {
      "name": "WBC Count",
      "value": 7.2,
      "unit": "10^9/L",
      "normalMinValue": 4.5,
      "normalMaxValue": 11
    }
  ],
  "notes": "All values within normal range.",
  "recommendConsultation": false
}

request.description:
Creates a new lab test result for a patient appointment. `appointmentId`, `testTypeId`, and `results` array are required. At least one parameter result must be provided in the `results` array.

Valid statuses: `pending`, `undergoing`, `completed`. Valid conditions: `normal`, `severe`, `unknown`.
Returns all test results in the system. Intended for admin/lab-tech overviews. May return a large dataset in production.
Returns all test results for a specific patient, sorted by most recent first. Used on the patient's health record / results history page.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the test result

request.description: Returns the full detail of a single test result record including all parameter values, condition assessment, and consultation recommendation.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the test result

request.description: Updates an existing test result. Typically used when a lab technician corrects values or updates the status from `undergoing` to `completed`.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the test result

request.description: Permanently deletes a test result record by ID. Irreversible. Returns 404 if not found.

item.name: Pharmacy – Medication Inventory
item.description:
Manages the pharmacy's medication stock (inventory). Each medication has a name, brand, strength, form (tablet/capsule/syrup/etc.), category, and one or more stock batches with expiry dates and quantities.

Note: These routes exist in the codebase but may not be mounted in the current server.js. Verify with the backend team before using in production. Base path assumed: `/api/pharmacy/medications`.

request.description: Simple health-check for the medication inventory route. Returns `{ ok: true }` if the route is reachable.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Paracetamol",
  "brandName": "Panadol",
  "strength": "500mg",
  "form": "tablet",
  "category": "Analgesic",
  "description": "Used for pain relief and fever reduction.",
  "unit": "tablets",
  "isActive": true
}

request.description: Creates a new medication entry in the inventory. `name`, `strength`, and `form` are required. Valid forms: `tablet`, `capsule`, `syrup`, `injection`, `cream`, `drops`, `other`. Batches are added separately after creation.
Returns all medication records sorted by most recently added. Each record includes a computed `totalQuantity` virtual field (sum of all batch quantities).
Returns the full medication record including all batch details, total quantity, and medication metadata.
Updates a medication record. Include only the fields to modify. Does not modify batches; use the batch endpoints to manage stock.
Permanently deletes a medication and all its batch records. Returns 404 if not found. Use with caution.
Adds a new stock batch to an existing medication. `batchNo`, `expiryDate`, `quantity`, `addedById`, and `addedByName` are required. The batch is embedded inside the medication document.
Updates a specific batch within a medication. Only include fields to change. The batch is identified by both the medication `id` and the batch `batchId`.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the batch to delete

request.description: Removes a specific stock batch from a medication. The total available stock will decrease accordingly. Returns 404 if the medication or batch is not found.

item.name: Pharmacy – Orders
item.description:
Manages pharmacy orders — the dispensing of medications to patients using a prescription as reference. Each order captures patient details, a prescription snapshot, and one or more medication items with quantity and batch allocation details.

Note: These routes exist in the codebase but may not be mounted in the current server.js. Verify with the backend team before using in production. Base path assumed: `/api/pharmacy/orders`.

request.description: Simple health-check for the pharmacy order route. Returns `{ ok: true }` if the route is reachable.

Creates a new pharmacy order for a patient based on a prescription. The server deducts stock from available batches (FIFO). `patient`, `prescriptionTextSnapshot`, and `items` are required.

If sufficient stock is available, status is `CONFIRMED`. If stock is insufficient, status becomes `WAITING_STOCK` and a notification may be sent.
Returns all pharmacy orders sorted by most recent first. Includes order number, patient details, status, items, and totals.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the pharmacy order

request.description: Returns the full details of a specific pharmacy order including all items, batch allocations, patient info, and totals.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the pharmacy order

request.description: Updates non-item fields of a pharmacy order such as status, patient contact details, or prescription snapshot. Does NOT restore or re-deduct stock. Valid statuses: `CONFIRMED`, `WAITING_STOCK`.

variable.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the pharmacy order

request.description: Updates the medication items in a pharmacy order. Previous stock deductions are restored first, then new quantities are re-deducted from available inventory. Use this when adjusting dispensed quantities after order creation.
